column1: # A baseline for tables/state_media_items.tsv: items of central state and Party media on Nvidia chips, Jan 1, 2024 to Jun 30, 2025, in that table's columns and by its rule: 49 rows (46 held: saved and read whole; 3 found: known and not saved). Made on Nov 25, 2026, row by row as each page was read. NOT A CENSUS, and gathered by other routes than that table: web searches; the saved pages of state outlets dated in those months; every item of those months in the index of the Yuyuan Tantian account on CCTV's site; and a scan of the titles of the daily editions of four papers (People's Daily, its Overseas Edition, Economic Daily, Guangming Daily), whose articles naming Nvidia were saved and read. The rows are kept apart: none is counted in tables/state_media_items.tsv. Scope, as that table's: one row per item of a central state or Party outlet (an item carried by several pages is one row, with the other carriers in column 10); commercial and local outlets only as carriers; items that do not name Nvidia or its chips are left out, and so are items that name Nvidia only in a passage on the world market (share prices, global demand, a new product, another country's deals) with nothing on Chinese buyers, the Chinese market, American curbs on China or Chinese alternatives. The items left out are in tables/state_media_baseline_outside_scope.tsv, each with its reason. Stance rule (that table's): warns = the item, in its own words or a speaker's it quotes, says Nvidia's chips carry security risks, or that Nvidia must prove them safe, or argues against buying or using them; mixed = that, together with words that Nvidia or American chipmakers are welcome or that imports may resume; a sentence that only reports or predicts buyers' reluctance is not a warning; welcomes (favours imports or Nvidia's presence); neutral (reports without advice); self-reliance (stresses home-made chips without advice on buying); other. Each stance was decided from the saved page read whole: 1 warns, 0 mixed, 4 welcome, 27 neutral, 13 self-reliance, 4 other. A second reading of 28 of the 46 held pages differed on three rows, none of them on a warning. Two flags stand at the start of the note (column 12): REPORTS-AUTHORITY = the item only reports an authority's act or words without comment, classed by the rule as written (6 rows); GROUP-PAPER = a paper of the People's Daily group that tables/state_media_items.tsv never holds (Securities Times, People's Tribune, China City News: 13 rows), so a comparison with that table counts the other 36.
